plain_english: Finds where the close sits within its 12-day low-to-high range, ranks it, and takes its 6-day correlation with volume's rank, flipped. Pushing to the top of the range on rising relative volume → short.
How far the perpetual future trades above spot. The funding rate is designed to push this gap back to zero.

Rank of how far today's high is above the lowest high of the last 2 days, raised to the power of the rank of the 6-day correlation between sector-relative vwap and subindustry-relative dollar volume, flipped. A bigger new high → more negative (short); the power term sets how much that counts.
How bumpy daily traded value (amount) was over 20 days (standard deviation).
How uneven volume-weighted price moves were over 5 days (std / mean).
Volume RSI (6-day): share of smoothed volume changes that were increases, x100.

Acts only when today's volume is above its 20-day average. Then it bets against the 7-day price change, harder when the move is unusually large versus the stock's own last 60 days: big drop → buy, big rise → short. Every quiet stock gets -1, the lowest score.
Rank of (high - 2-day min high) raised to the rank of the 6-day correlation between vwap and 120-day average volume, flipped.
Rank of the 1-day vwap change raised to the time-series rank of the close vs 50-day average volume correlation.

For each of the last 5 days, take the close if the stock rose or the 20-day volatility if it fell, square it, and find the day with the largest value. A squared price always beats a squared volatility, so this really finds the week's highest up-day close. Score = which day that was, ranked and centered on 0. Read as "days since the peak", a fresh peak scores low (short); code that counts the other way turns it into momentum.

The larger of two signals, flipped: the rank of the smoothed 4-day change in vwap, and where the smoothed 2-day percentage drop of an open/low blend sits in its last 16 days. Shorts stocks that moved a lot either way recently, so it is hard to read cleanly.
The same recipe as #58 at the industry level with longer windows (4-day correlation, 16-day smoothing, 8-day time rank). It mixes vwap with itself (0.73 × vwap + 0.27 × vwap), which is just vwap.
How uneven volume-weighted price moves were over 20 days (std / mean).
